headline: Medium-risk pair: shared file/workspace and API-backed RAG create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways; no direct evidence of isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress can install packages and has no documented isolation surface, while Kotaemon reads files in a web UI and calls external APIs. If Botpress outputs are copied into Kotaemon’s document/chat inputs, attacker-controlled text can be treated as instructions. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented capabilities, not directly observed.
conditions: IF Botpress output is pasted or saved into Kotaemon inputs
IF Kotaemon ingests Botpress-generated text as trusted document content
mitigations: Use a separate staging folder for Botpress outputs
Disable copy-paste of untrusted agent text into Kotaemon
Add a manual review step before ingestion
Tag Botpress-generated content as untrusted in filenames
requires-engineering: add provenance filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kotaemon explicitly handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and writes to ./ktem_app_data; Botpress has no egress, but its outputs can still carry sensitive content into Kotaemon’s storage or API calls. The shared-data path is plausible through operator transfer or a common workspace, so leakage risk is real though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs contain secrets or customer data
IF those outputs are stored in Kotaemon’s ./ktem_app_data or sent through its API-backed connectors
mitigations: Keep Botpress and Kotaemon on separate workspaces
Do not place secrets in Botpress prompts or outputs
Rotate any API keys exposed to Kotaemon
Review ./ktem_app_data permissions before use
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on inter-agent transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and Kotaemon supports multiple instances plus Docker privileges and file-backed state. Even without explicit shared-write evidence, both can mutate local resources if co-located, creating overwrite or state-conflict risk. Uncertainty about the exact deployment should escalate to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents run on the same host or shared directory
IF Botpress package installs or Kotaemon file writes target overlapping paths
mitigations: Run each agent in its own container
Use distinct working directories
Avoid shared mutable volumes
Check for concurrent writes before starting both
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestration locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kotaemon is a RAG-style system that can render or act on retrieved content, while Botpress can generate arbitrary support text. If Botpress output is fed into Kotaemon without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream answers or actions. The interaction is plausible from the profiles, but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Kotaemon uses Botpress output as authoritative context
IF no human or automated verification step checks Botpress claims before reuse
mitigations: Require source citations before reuse
Insert a human review gate
Compare Botpress claims against original documents
Limit Botpress output to summaries only
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and rejection rules

E_compliance.rationale: Kotaemon explicitly handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and may send content to third-party APIs; Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented residency or retention controls. If EU PII or regulated support data flows from Botpress into Kotaemon’s API-backed processing, compliance mismatch is plausible. Botpress lacks documented controls, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF regulated customer-support data is processed by both agents
IF Kotaemon forwards that data to non-approved external APIs
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-regulated data
Disable external API connectors for regulated workflows
Document retention settings for Kotaemon
Review data residency before deployment
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing by data class
